messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a complete, playable 3D open-world shooter with weapon selection, multiplayer-style server capacity, building, and character skins; the user additionally requested weapon crates that open to swap weapons.

## Requirements
- User described servers supporting up to 25 players and gameplay inspired by Fortnite shooting and Minecraft building.
- Include a small menu for selecting skins/characters.
- Add boxes that players can open to swap weapons.
- No clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions.

## Decisions
- Implemented a browser-based Three.js first-person shooter prototype with AI rivals and a displayed 12/25 server count; multiplayer is simulated locally rather than networked.
- Added weapon crates, weapon inventory, buildable cover, skin selection, desktop and touch controls.

## Work State
### Completed
- Created a playable game in `index.html`, including a lobby, character selection, open-world terrain, AI opponents, weapons, crates, building, HUD, and responsive controls.
- Extracted the module script and validated syntax with `node --check`.
- Opened the game in Playwright and captured/read a JPEG screenshot; clicked Deploy to check gameplay.

### Active
- None.

### Blocked
- None. Browser screenshot showed the game rendering; no visual issues were reported.

## Next Move
1. Optionally inspect gameplay more thoroughly and fix any discovered runtime or visual defects.
2. Consider clarifying that multiplayer is not actually networked if reporting implementation limitations.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Entire game implementation.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- The development server was started with `python3 -m http.server 3002`.
- Playwright console contained a missing `/favicon.ico` 404 and WebGL readback performance warnings.

content.text:
Built the playable 3D shooter in `index.html`. It includes a character/skin menu, open terrain, AI rivals, weapon selection and crate swaps, buildable cover, health/shields, and desktop and touch controls.

**Assumption:** The server count is a lobby-style display; this prototype uses local AI opponents, not actual networked multiplayer. Syntax checks passed, and I verified the game renders and deploys in the browser.
